stem: A nurse reports a recurring workplace safety hazard to the employer and then files a safety complaint with OSHA. The nurse is later threatened with discipline specifically because of the report. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: Section 11(c) of the OSH Act prohibits retaliation for protected workplace-safety activities such as raising safety concerns or filing an OSHA complaint, and a worker who experiences retaliation should contact OSHA promptly
options.B: Employers may discipline workers solely for filing a workplace-safety complaint because reporting hazards is not a protected activity
options.C: OSHA whistleblower protections guarantee a promotion or financial reward whenever a worker reports a hazard
options.D: Section 11(c) protects only physicians and does not apply to other covered employees such as nurses

rationale: OSHA states that Section 11(c) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act prohibits retaliation against employees for exercising protected workplace-safety rights, including raising safety concerns with an employer, filing a safety and health complaint with OSHA, participating in an OSHA inspection, or reporting a work-related injury or illness. A worker who believes retaliation occurred should contact OSHA promptly because filing deadlines apply. Protection does not guarantee a reward or immunity from legitimate nonretaliatory employment actions.
educational_objective: Recognize federal anti-retaliation protection for employees who engage in protected workplace-safety reporting under OSH Act Section 11(c).
source_document_title: Worker Participation; OSHA Online Whistleblower Complaint Form
source_locator: Worker Participation: Section 11(c) prohibits retaliation for filing an OSHA safety complaint, raising safety concerns, participating in an inspection, or reporting work-related injury/illness; whistleblower complaint information explains adverse action and filing requirements
source_claim_supported: Covered employees are protected from employer retaliation for specified workplace-safety activities under OSH Act Section 11(c); retaliation complaints are subject to filing requirements.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — legal responsibilities, advocacy and workplace safety
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — protected workplace-safety reporting
correction_summary: Replaced the vague claim that generic whistleblower laws protect every good-faith report. Limited the final item to a specific federal statute, Section 11(c), and protected workplace-safety activities within OSHA's authority.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current OSHA Section 11(c) worker-participation and complaint guidance verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Protected safety reporting, anti-retaliation rule and prompt filing requirement are official-source supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; safety reporting is protected activity.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; protection is anti-retaliation, not guaranteed reward.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately states the federal protection without overclaim.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices interpret the same retaliation scenario.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked patient-safety versus worker-safety jurisdiction, statute-specific filing periods and legitimate employer actions; stem expressly limits the issue to OSHA workplace-safety reporting.
